definition: OpenClaw is a free and open-source autonomous artificial intelligence agent that can execute tasks via large language models (LLMs), using messaging platforms as its main user interface.
details: OpenClaw is a free and open-source autonomous artificial intelligence agent that can execute tasks via large language models (LLMs), using messaging platforms as its main user interface.

explainer.lead: OpenClaw is a free and open-source autonomous AI agent that executes tasks via large language models, using messaging platforms as its main user interface. Its rapid renaming and viral popularity made it a notable case of fast-moving open-source agent projects.

tiers.eli5: It is a free robot helper that you talk to through a chat app, and it goes off and does tasks for you.
tiers.practitioner: Developed by Peter Steinberger and first published in November 2025 as Warelay, derived from his assistant Clawd; it was renamed Moltbot on January 27, 2026 after trademark complaints by Anthropic and OpenClaw three days later. The pitfall is building on a project whose name and identity can change abruptly.
tiers.paperLevel: An open-source autonomous agent driven by large language models with messaging platforms as its primary interface. Adoption is measured in repository activity: 247,000 stars and 47,700 forks on GitHub as of March 2, 2026.

explainer.example: Its viral popularity coincided with Moltbook, a social networking service launched by Matt Schlicht intended for AI agents such as OpenClaw; some Chinese developers have adapted it to work with other systems.
